key_insight: Steric and solvation control enables hybrid perovskite monolayers exceeding 1000 µm² in lateral area, supporting lithography-free, low-static-power optoelectronics.
engineering_relevance: Large ultrathin crystals permit solvent-free contacts through physical shadow masks, avoiding solvent-induced degradation during conventional lithography.
method: Use a ternary-solvent strategy combining alcohol cosolvents and an amine additive to suppress out-of-plane stacking.
Tune precursor solvation and solvent volatility to sustain edge-mediated growth during annealing.
Fabricate planar devices from isolated ultrathin (PEA)₂PbI₄ channels using shadow-mask contacts.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports (PEA)₂CuCl₄ monolayers exceeding 1000 µm² and (PEA)₂PbI₄ devices with dark currents of 10⁻¹⁵–10⁻¹³ A, approximately 0.2 pW static power at 5 V, and a light-to-dark current ratio of 430.
watch_item: Scalable manufacturing still requires validation of monolayer yield, device-to-device uniformity, and long-term operational stability.
paper_title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
